top.title: The USMNT needs Copa América. What it doesn't need is another home game
top.description: USA fans look on from the stands during the CONMEBOL Copa America match between the United States and Boliva on June 23, 2024 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Copa América, South American soccer’s pride and joy, is returning to the U.S. in 2028 because organizers remain spellbound by the ticket sales and marketing success of the 2024 edition here. Tuesday’s announcement is a positive development for the U.S. team, which, for competitive reasons, desperately needs a break from the monotony of CONCACAF before the 2030 World Cup. Only so much is gained from fiddling with neighbors over and over again. Assuming the U.S. qualifies next summer, Copa América will furnish its to-be-announced head coach with pressure-packed, consequential matches in a prestigious tournament against different types of opponents. That’s a welcome change from the Nations Leagues and biennial Gold Cups, which are starting to feel like watching “Friends” reruns on Nick at Nite. But here’s where this Copa news falls short for the U.S. program: It’s in the U.S. again. Yes, the team needs to play in Copa América, but what it really needs is to play in it in South America. It needs to step out of its comfort zone of sterile hotels and stadiums. It needs to say goodbye to family and friends, experience new training and playing environments, and feel the heat of stepping into Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã or Buenos Aires’ El Monumental to play the host team. True, the U.S. often feels like the visiting team at home when it tangles with Latin American opponents boasting a passionate diaspora. But the players still enjoy the predictability of home logistics, travel patterns, security and general nationwide support. That is not what they need right now. They need to suffer. Consider this: The U.S. hardly ever plays outside its borders, an arrangement that many might argue has left the program soft heading into World Cups. Talent, tactics and such are part of why the U.S. has stumbled in the round of 16 in its past four appearances, but mental toughness in the pressure-cookers of knockout soccer can’t be dismissed either. The location of matches is often out of the U.S.’s control. For revenue purposes, CONCACAF has staged every Nations League final four and almost every Gold Cup in the States. CONMEBOL, which oversees South American soccer, has shifted Copa América — the oldest international tournament in the world — to the U.S. three of the past five times after staging the first 44 editions in its own continent. The U.S. does have a say in the location of friendlies. Here again, though, the team is not facing the rigors of playing away matches. It has played 16 consecutive friendlies in FIFA windows at home since a visit to Mexico in October 2024. Going back to 2022, the number grows to 28 of 31. The five-time major champion came back this year under the “Returning Member Program” after securing his exit from a LIV Golf contract. With Koepka ending at No. 108 in the FedEx Cup, three other golfers advanced one position in the final rankings. top.title: Scarlett Schremmer Disqualified From Annika Debut After Lying
top.description: Michael Madrid-Imagn Images The 19-year-old University of Miami sophomore received a rare sponsor exemption to The Annika driven by Gainbridge, only to disqualify herself by lying about a yardage book. She claimed she never used the illegal green-reading material when officials first asked, but photographic evidence proved otherwise. Golfmagic reported the disqualification came Saturday after the tour saw clear images of her consulting the prohibited book during the round. The book itself was legal in college golf, which explains why it sat in her bag, but it carries zero weight on the professional tour. Schremmer missed the cut before the ruling dropped, yet the lie turned a missed opportunity into a scandal. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, caddied for her, adding a layer of personal pressure that clearly backfired. Social media saw playing partner Perrine Delacour publicly challenge the tournament’s rule breach handling, causing the situation to become messy. The Lie That Sealed Her Fate Officials were alerted to the issue after the opening round, yet Schremmer kept playing on Friday before the truth came out. She initially told officials the book was not in use, a claim she later admitted was false in a Friday Instagram post. Schremmer wrote, “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.” That panic cost her the chance to show her skills against the best women in the world. Delacour, who partnered Schremmer for the first two rounds, took to X to ask, “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” The French veteran confirmed she spoke directly to rules officials about the violation, highlighting how the amateur status of the invitee complicated the situation. The LPGA Tour stated the rule requires players to use only approved books throughout their round, and photo evidence showed Schremmer violated that mandate. Trust Is Hard To Build Back With two fall college tournament wins and a USGA 2026 Elite Amateur Program spot secured, Schremmer held the 51st rank in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. Those credentials meant nothing once she chose to hide the truth. While Schremmer’s Friday admission signaled a move from denial to accountability, the harm remains irreversible. She stated in her post, according to Yahoo, “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

top.title: Measles death toll rises to 14 as national case tally nears 6,000
top.description: Last week, international health authorities formally announced that the US had lost its measles-elimination status, meaning that the virus is once again endemic. But the official determination is a bit like getting the technical readout of a cracked dam while the country is already feet under water. The national tally of measles cases is nearing 6,000 for the year, the highest count since 1991. Transmission is widespread, with 47 states and jurisdictions reporting cases. There have been 43 outbreaks this year, which account for 96 percent of the cases. Four states have case counts above 500, including Pennsylvania, which leads with 1,638 cases as of November 23 . Nearly 650 people have been hospitalized nationwide. As of today, 14 people have died. Deaths and transmission On November 23, Pennsylvania's health department announced its ninth confirmed death, an unvaccinated resident of Centre County. On November 24, Wisconsin reported its third measles death , an adult in Lafayette County. The report follows two other deaths in the state, an infant and a child . New York has also reported a death, which was of a 7-month-old baby . On November 20, Virginia reported the death of a young child between the age of 0 and 4 . Read full article Comments

top.title: 'Go be somewhere else': Steelers legend challenges DK Metcalf
top.description: Credit: The Pivot Sports After a strong start to the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have lost back-to-back games coming off the bye, and star receiver DK Metcalf is once again sucking up oxygen around the team in on-field confrontations. During Sunday’s loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Metcalf was ejected for poking Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. The incident came after key drops and a build-up of physicality with the Philadelphia secondary throughout the game. Metcalf had just one reception for 2 yards, his third time in the past four contests with two or fewer catches. The former Seahawk is set to make $38-plus million starting next season, putting a glaring spotlight on his lack of productivity and professionalism and leading former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin to check Metcalf on Sunday Night Football after the ejection. During an episode of The Pivot Sports to start the week, fellow Steelers great Ryan Clark added to the criticism of Metcalf, calling out the star for his lack of “emotional regulation” and questioning whether Metcalf was long for Pittsburgh. “Why do we have to be the guy that can’t control himself? That has no professional maturity. That doesn’t understand emotional regulation,” Clark said. “Then you get disqualified, and you shake your head.” Clark showed several of Metcalf’s earlier miscues in the game, contrasting the star’s lack of focus with how his backup, Max Hurleman, played as well as the clutch performance of Philadelphia’s DeVonta Smith on the other side. Clark emphasized how much Metcalf’s mistakes cost the team. “Maybe throw hands when you’re getting locked up. Maybe throw hands when you’re trying to get a block. Maybe throw hands when it’s 3rd-and-4, and you need to get four yards. But you want to do it after the play?” Clark said. “Slapping the referee, that doesn’t make you a bad man. That makes you a man that eventually goes home.” The incident with DeJean also opened Metcalf and the Steelers up to media chatter and off-field distractions . Later, Clark highlighted numerous Steelers greats from the team’s two Super Bowl runs in the late 2000s and early 2010s, challenging Metcalf to match their mental toughness and leadership. “Most of the games, they were all available. And what they did was lead,” he said. “They would never walk out on their team after being kicked out of a game, without hearing what the coach had to say, without hearing what their teammates had to say. Be accountable, DK. Lead, DK. Be the person that they brought you over there to be. And if not, go be somewhere else.” To make matters worse for the Steelers, after acquiring Metcalf, the team ultimately turned him into the replacement for former Pittsburgh draft pick George Pickens. top.title: Tsunami RT Brings Porsche To IMSA GTD Class For 2027 Season
top.description: Manthey racing�s Porsche 911 (911) is a blur of speed up from turn 5 during practice at the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix Featuring IMSA, Friday, July 31, 2026, at Road America near Elkhart Lake, Wis. Tsunami RT is heading to the United States to race. The San Marino-based team will field a Porsche 911 GT3 R in the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup starting in 2027. This move brings a new name to the GTD class and adds depth to the five-race schedule. Team principal Valerio M. Speziali wants to build a lasting presence in North America. He sees the US market as a place to grow the team’s skills over time. “We are delighted to join the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup next year, giving us the chance to build our experience and grow in endurance racing season by season,” Speziali said, according to Speedway Digest . The group knows the competition is fierce, but they are not backing down. “We know how competitive the GTD field is and we’re ready to fight for strong results from the opening round,” he added according to Speedway Digest. A Driver Mix Built for Endurance The car will carry the number 79 and feature a mix of veterans and fresh talent. Fabio Babini leads the group with deep roots in IMSA history. He won the GTU class at the 2000 Rolex 24 and took the GT title at Le Mans in 2001. His last start in the WeatherTech Championship was back in 2019, but he knows the track well. Matteo Cressoni brings recent experience with 13 starts between 2015 and 2025 in various GT cars. Two new faces will make their debut in 2027. Alex Fontana and Johannes Zelger have raced together for Tsunami RT in the Intercontinental GT Challenge during the 2026 season. The team will rotate drivers based on the race length. They plan to use a three-driver lineup for the Sebring, Glen, Road America, and Road Atlanta events. This strategy helps manage the physical toll of long races while keeping speed high. Adding a new Porsche entry changes the dynamic of the GTD class. The field is already crowded with top-tier teams, and every new car adds pressure. Babini’s resume shows the team is not just playing for participation. He has won at the highest levels of sports car racing. His experience in the GRAND-AM series and American Le Mans Series gives the team a solid foundation. Cressoni has also seen action in Ferrari and Lamborghini entries, proving he can handle different machines. The Rolex 24 holds special weight for this organization. Speziali called the chance to see the team on the entry list a major milestone. It is not just about finishing the race. It is about proving that a European team can succeed in the tough US endurance scene. The 2027 season will show if they have the pace to match the big names. According to Speedway Digest, the 2027 IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship will mark Tsunami RT’s debut with a Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) competing across the five-race IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup schedule.

The substitute nodded in with 13 minutes left to break Villa's resistance, scoring with the game's first effort on target. It settled a scrappy match and dented Villa's top-eight ambitions, with Emery's side having lost in Barcelona earlier this month. Villa knew victory in Turkey - as they returned to Istanbul for the first time since winning the Europa League in May - would put them on track to reach the knockout stages automatically. But defeats leaves their hopes in the balance and they now face tough home games against champions Paris St-Germain on 8 December before Borussia Dortmund come to Villa Park in January, with Villa then finishing the league phase at Slavia Prague. They are now winless in six games in all competitions having failed to score in four of them. Emery would initially have been satisfied how his team handled the surface - after much debate about the condition of the pitch - and the atmosphere at the RAMS Stadium. Without star striker Victor Osimhen, sidelined with a knee injury, the hosts struggled for a focal point allowing Tyrone Mings and Victor Lindelof to comfortably hold off any muted attacks. Yet Villa themselves struggled to create until Ian Maatsen was thwarted by some desperate home defending early in the second half. It was Villa's best and only chance as the hosts took control and snatched the winner when Gul pounced after Villa failed to clear a corner. top.title: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato
top.description: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Two days before Thanksgiving, the Philadelphia Phillies have not made a significant roster move of any kind. The December 1 lockout is looming, and the Phillies are beginning to run out of time to make moves. But it's not just the time crunch making things tricky for the Phillies. They've already lost out on Teruaki Sato, easily the best free-agent option the Phillies could've landed this Fall. He's headed to the Chicago Cubs on a six-year, $120 million deal. After missing out on Sato, what now for the Phillies' offseason plans? The Athletic's Charlotte Varnes and Matt Gelb shared an update on just that, and it's looking like the Phillies could be in for quite the bleak offseason. Phillies might be in for a bleak offseason after missing out on Teruaki Sato After missing out on Sato, it would seem natural for the Phillies to look towards Seiya Suzuki and/or Randy Arozarena as free-agent outfield options. But, as The Athletic duo pointed out, there are problems with both. "The Phillies would have to sacrifice draft picks and international bonus money to sign either outfielder because both were extended qualifying offers," Varnes and Gelb write. "They may wait to sign until the labor situation is resolved." There's just one problem with that line of thinking: "If Arozarena's market develops in the next week, though, the Phillies will not have the luxury of waiting," Varnes and Gelb write. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Between the loss of draft picks and international bonus pool money, and the potentially rushed nature of a Suzuki or Arozarena deal, the Phillies might not be the landing spots for either right-handed hitting outfielder. So, if they aren't a perfect suitor for an outfielder, what about a pitcher to upgrade the bullpen? Unfortunately, things aren't looking good there either. "They could focus on pitching, but the Phillies, according to multiple league sources, are not considered serious players for the top free-agent reliever, Adrian Morejon," Gelb and Varnes report. Adrian Morejon would've been an awesome pickup as a setup man for Jhoan Duran. But a deal isn't looking likely. With issues signing someone like Suzuki or Arozarena, and their lack of strong interest in Morejon, what could they actually do this offseason? top.title: Blue Jays land Japanese star pitcher Kaima Taira on $80M deal
top.description: Blue Jays signing The Blue Jays landed a starting pitcher for roughly one-sixth the price of Tarik Skubal. After losing to the Mets in the Skubal sweepstakes, the Blue Jays pivoted and are signing Japanese righty Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million deal, The Post’s Jon Heyman first reported . The deal includes an opt-out clause after the third year, per Heyman. Kaima Taira of the Seibu Lions celebrates setting an NPB record with 39 consecutive scoreless games in Fukuoka, Japan, Thursday, July 1, 2021. /Kyodo News via AP The starting pitching dominos are falling in free agency ahead of the expected Dec. 1 lockout, with Skubal serving as the catalyst by signing his nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets . The Blue Jays made a competitive nine-year, $420 million offer for Skuba l, but he opted for $30 million more to head to Flushing. Freddy Peralta agreed to a five-year, $125 million deal with the Orioles on Tuesday, and the pitching-needy Blue Jays swooped in to land the talented 27-year-old Taira. Taira has experience as a reliever and starter, and spent the past season with the Seibu Lions of the Japan Pacific League as a starter. He posted a 1.54 ERA spanning 23 outings, pitching 146 innings and striking out 141 batters. Taira walked 45 batters but allowed just four homers. The year prior, he made 54 appearances and tallied 52 2/3 innings while posting a 2.05 ERA. He owns a career 1.85 ERA in his nine seasons pitching in Japan, according to Baseball Reference. “His stuff and release characteristics are what is intriguing to evaluators. His fastball sits 94-97 mph and hits 100 mph with his four-seam fastball, the headliner in an eight-pitch mix: sinker, changeup, splitter, cutter, slider, sweeper, and curveball,” according to ESPN . “Taira achieves a unique low release and advantageous angle for his fastball with his outlier extension (roughly a foot more than his 5-foot-8 stature) and lower than average arm slot.” The Blue Jays now have a solid rotation featuring AL Cy Young runner-up Dylan Cease, Taira, midseason trade acquisition righty Joel Soriano and talented youngster Trey Yesavage. They reportedly are also in the mix for offensive help and their representatives met with Jazz Chisholm Jr. earlier in free agency. Toronto finished in last place in the AL East last year following its run to the World Series in 2025.

top.description: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect This offseason has gotten off to a busy start for the Minnesota Twins. Although a lockout appears to be looming , that hasn’t stopped Tom Pohlad from backing up his talk when it comes to spending money. Ryan Jeffers secured the first windfall of cash by accepting the qualifying offer at $23.15 million for 2027. Sonny Gray then returned to the franchise on a two-year deal worth $55 million. What portion of those salaries will be paid remains to be seen. It’s also possible that the Pohlads won’t be the ones writing the checks after all. Walters still expects Pohlads to sell the Minnesota Twins After the 2024 season, the Pohlads gave Minnesota Twins fans the best news in years. They were exploring a sale . Then they pulled the team off the market before Tom Pohlad took over for his younger brother Joe. Since then, Tom has been adamant about the family’s plan to re-invest in the organization in ways that those before him have not. He has also downplayed any plans to put the team back up for sale after a new Collective Bargaining Agreement is reached. However, local insider Charley Walters (Pioneer Press) remains convinced that is the ultimate endgame. I remain convinced that once baseball settles on a new labor deal, the Twins will be sold. The Pohlad ownership “explored” _ their word _ a sale in October of 2024 before announcing in August of 2025 the team would remain under their control. No doubt Twins’ ownership figures a new labor contract that will include major TV deals across the league will be worth a lot more than the $1.75 billion they quietly sought last year, probably even more than $2 billion. The Twins scenario is not unlike Angels’ owner Arte Moreno announcing in 2022 that he was “exploring” a potential sale, then pulling the team off the market a year later. Then, last September, he agreed to sell for a record $4 billion. Charley Walters – Don’t Print That Related: Don’t Laugh. top.title: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions
top.description: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions Fran Soto, president of Spain’s Technical Committee of Referees (CTA), has expressed his desire to improve relations with Real Madrid amid ongoing tensions. Los Blancos have been vociferous in their complaints about the refereeing in Spain as well as the Negreira scandal involving Barcelona, leading to a lot of tension between the club and the governing bodies. Soto wants to move on from the Negreira scandal Speaking to the media at the first Refereeing Gala, Soto addressed the ongoing tensions surrounding the refereeing in Spain and Real Madrid’s complaints, in particular. The CTA president defended the refereeing community over the fallout from the Negreira scandal and called for the focus to shift towards restoring normality. “The referees are the ones most harmed by a person who was vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees,” Soto said, as quoted by SPORT . Real Madrid are unhappy with the refereeing in Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Soto insisted that officials have suffered the consequences of the controversy and argued that they cannot remain trapped by events from the past. ”We mustn’t dwell on the past; we have to move forward and continue refereeing, put it behind us, and look to the future,” he added. Soto questions Real Madrid’s VAR statistics Soto was also asked about the presentation made by Real Madrid during the club’s recent assembly , wherein they showed that VAR had ruled out 42 of their goals since the technology was introduced, compared to 19 for Barcelona. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez used the figures to reinforce the club’s complaints about what it considers unfavourable refereeing treatment. Real Madrid have made multiple complaints over the officiating. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) Soto declined to engage in a direct confrontation with Real Madrid but questioned whether the figures, on their own, could support the conclusions being drawn. “Every club defends its position. I don’t agree that this objective data can be used to draw conclusions,” he stated. However, the CTA president made clear that he has no intention of escalating the dispute and would prefer to see communication between the two sides return to normal. “I don’t want to get into a dispute with any club, least of all with Madrid. I hope that in the future we can resolve this situation,” he concluded.

nigeria.title: Omo-Agege attack: Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused the All Progressives Congress (APC) of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the 2027 general elections, following the killing of six people in an attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Delta State. The organisation said the attack on the campaign entourage of former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, exposed the dangers of allowing political violence to flourish ahead of the elections, warning that it could undermine peaceful electoral competition. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, the MDPCO condemned the November 23 incident, alleging that APC agents were responsible for the attack in Delta State. It warned that the incident could be part of a broader attempt to deploy armed thugs against opposition parties and frustrate the conduct of peaceful elections. The organisation said, “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters ahead of the 2023 elections that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ The campaign organisation also cited an alleged threat by Edo State APC Chairman, Jarret Tenebe, to invoke the power of AK-47 against anyone who opposed the party’s plan to secure Tinubu’s re-election, accusing the ruling party of failing to condemn the statement. It further alleged that opposition parties had suffered attacks in Sokoto, Kebbi, Edo, Lagos, Cross River, Kaduna and Kano states, describing the latest incident in Delta as part of a disturbing pattern. The MDPCO accused the APC leadership of failing to take decisive action against members allegedly involved in political violence, warning that its silence could further embolden those responsible. “This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition,” it said. The organisation warned that Nigerians would not accept the use of violence or insecurity as instruments of electoral conquest, insisting that political parties must respect citizens’ freedom to choose their leaders. It declared that the resort to violence would not alter what it described as Nigerians’ determination to vote the APC out of power. “The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said. It demanded an immediate end to what it described as attempts to suppress democratic participation, while urging Nigerians to support its principal, Engr. Seyi Makinde

nigeria.title: It was reprisal action – Ughelli LG chairman accuses Omo-Agege’s boys of firing first shot
nigeria.description: The Chairman of Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, Jaro Movudu, has described the violence involving Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and his supporters as a reprisal, accusing the senator’s men of killing community members before the incident escalated. Movudu, who had earlier been accused by Omo-Agege of masterminding an alleged assassination attempt on the senator, denied the allegation, claiming that the violence was triggered by the killing of the community’s president-general and other residents. Speaking on Channels Television on Tuesday, the council chairman alleged that Omo-Agege’s supporters fired the first shots, killing members of the community where the senator held his campaign rally. He said the incident was a sad development, extending condolences to victims on both sides of the violence, regardless of their political affiliations. “Let me express my sincere condolences to all those who lost their lives yesterday on both sides. Most of them know to me. They are my friends. Whether they are working for NDC or APC, nobody’s life is worth the ambition of anybody, and it was a sad day yesterday,” he said. Movudu alleged that Omo-Agege had made provocative remarks against him during his campaign visit to the community, claiming that the senator allegedly incited his supporters before they opened fire. He said he was not present at the venue when the campaign took place, as he was in his office, but alleged that Omo-Agege abused him while addressing residents and subsequently riled up his supporters. “But when he was leaving, he riled up the people. He gave instructions to his boys, and then they gunned down the president-general of the community and then shut other people down. It was that death that brought that anger,” Movudu alleged. The council chairman described the subsequent violence as a reprisal for the killing, claiming that the community was angered by the death of its leader and other innocent residents. “What happened yesterday was a reprisal action to answer to the unjust killing of the president and two other onlookers who were innocent,” he said. Reacting to Omo-Agege’s claim that he was targeted for assassination, Movudu questioned the presence of firearms at the senator’s campaign rally, alleging that his supporters were armed. “At the end of it all, he came to TV and was saying that they wanted to kill him. You don’t go to campaign rallies with AK-47. You don’t go to campaign rallies with pump-action rifles. What are you going to use them for?” he asked. Movudu further questioned why supporters attending a political rally would be carrying weapons, alleging that the firearms were used against members of the community. “The people that are going to vote for you, you want to kill them?” he said. His allegations come amid conflicting accounts of the violence, with Omo-Agege accusing Movudu of orchestrating an assassination attempt against him during his campaign visit to Delta community. nigeria.title: 2027: Yari urges Zamfara voters to back APC candidates
nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau The Director-General of President Bola Tinubu’s Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has urged voters in Zamfara State to support All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels in the 2027 general elections. Yari made the appeal on Monday at the flag-off of the re-election campaign of Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, in Talata Mafara, headquarters of Talata Mafara Local Government Area. The unit, called 61st Parallel Asset Management, is expected to start operating by early December, CEO Nathan McCauley said in an interview to CoinDesk. Its first product will be a bitcoin-denominated fund, meaning returns are measured in BTC rather than dollars. The name nods to the city of Anchorage, Alaska, which sits at 61 degrees north latitude. “We have increasingly heard clients say they want to earn on top of the assets they hold at Anchorage — something that’s very common among the large financial institutions of the world,” McCauley said. Anchorage has filed a Form ADV, the disclosure document investment advisers use to register with the Securities and Exchange Commission or state regulators, or to report as exempt advisers. The form covers a firm’s ownership, business, assets under management, fees and conflicts of interest. As of Tuesday afternoon, the SEC’s public adviser database showed no record for 61st Parallel, so the filing’s details were not yet public. Paperwork dating back to summer The entity itself is not new. New York state records show that 61st Parallel Asset Management LLC, a Delaware company, registered to do business in New York on July 8, listing an office on Park Avenue South in Manhattan. Anchorage already lets clients earn on some holdings. Its website lists staking, which pays rewards for helping secure proof-of-stake networks, and a separate rewards product for eligible assets. Bitcoin runs on proof-of-work and cannot be staked natively. Anchorage has not said publicly how the fund will generate yield, what it will charge or which clients will qualify. Common ways to earn on it include lending coins out, posting them as collateral or selling options against them, and each carries its own risk. business.title: Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coldcard Postmortem Says Weak Seeds, Not Hacked Devices, Drove Bitcoin Thefts Coinkite on Tuesday published its full postmortem on the Coldcard seed-generation flaw that let thieves drain bitcoin from customer wallets starting in July, saying no device was hacked and that the stolen keys were rebuilt offline from weak seeds. The 18-page report , dated Nov. 23 and modeled on a National Transportation Safety Board accident report, lays out how the defect shipped in Coldcard firmware from March 29, 2021, through July 30, 2026, and why years of outside reviews missed it. “The losses are real and, for some customers, life-changing. No report or firmware update can undo that. We are sorry,” Coinkite wrote. A silent swap in the random number generator A seed is the list of recovery words that controls a bitcoin wallet, and it is only as safe as the randomness used to create it. Coldcard devices were supposed to draw that randomness from the hardware random number generator built into their STM32 chip. Instead, a firmware setting switched that hardware source off, and a safeguard in Coinkite’s libNgU code library failed to catch it. Seed generation quietly fell back to Yasmarang, a predictable software generator built into MicroPython, the programming environment the firmware runs on. Nothing crashed, and the devices produced normal-looking seed words. Coinkite estimates affected seeds carried roughly 40 bits of effective security on the older Mk2 and Mk3 models and about 72 bits on the Mk4, Mk5 and Q, against an intended 128 bits. That shrinks the pool of possible seeds enough for attackers to search it offline. The report says Coinkite’s release checks confirmed the hardware code was present, but never confirmed that seed generation actually reached it. At least 15 independent review efforts since 2021 also missed the flaw, including two paid third-party reviews and an AI-assisted firmware review this year that produced 85 candidate findings. Hundreds of Coldcard owners report losses Unexpected transactions from affected seeds began July 29. Coinkite said it identified the defect the next day, after users discovered thefts, and shipped fixed firmware for every supported release track on July 31. As of Nov. 18, Coinkite had received about 300 loss-related support tickets tied to 242 customer accounts, or about 0.21% of its estimated Coldcard user base. The company’s blog post cites 236 accounts. Because Coldcard is self-custodial, Coinkite can only count losses that customers report, and it says the true number is likely higher. The report cites Galaxy Research figures showing 1,778.84 BTC stolen from more than 8,600 addresses, worth about $107 million at today’s price. Galaxy pegged losses above $115 million in August, based on prices when the coins were taken, and white hats later moved some exposed coins into a recovery trust. business.title: UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65%
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine UniCredit Opens Bitcoin to Italian Savers, Capping Gains at 65% UniCredit on Tuesday began selling a capital-protected certificate that lets retail clients in Italy follow the bitcoin price, a product the bank calls the first investment solution of its kind in the country. The six-year, euro-denominated certificate will be listed on the Munich stock exchange and is linked to the iShares Bitcoin ETP managed by BlackRock, UniCredit said in a release. The placement period runs from Nov. 24 to Dec. 18, 2026. The note is open only to UniCredit Italia retail clients with specific characteristics, and only through the bank’s advisory service. It can’t be bought independently or by investors who aren’t UniCredit clients, and the minimum investment is €1,000, Italian newswire Teleborsa reported . How the certificate works A capital-protected certificate is a structured note. The issuing bank promises to repay the original investment at maturity and pays a return tied to an underlying asset, in this case bitcoin through the BlackRock product. Buyers hold a claim on the bank, not bitcoin itself. If bitcoin is down at maturity, holders get 100% of their capital back. If it rises, they share in the gain up to a maximum return of 65% on the capital invested. Before maturity, the certificate’s price follows market conditions, so the protection applies only at the end of the six years. That cap works out to roughly 8.7% a year at most, no matter how far bitcoin climbs. And because the certificate is UniCredit’s own debt, the protection depends on the bank’s ability to pay. Documents for a similar UniCredit note in Germany state that no third-party guarantee covers an issuer default. “With the launch of this certificate, UniCredit is writing a new page of financial innovation in the country, confirming its market leadership,” said Chicco Di Stasi, Head of Group Investment Product Solutions at UniCredit. “Diversification is no longer just a prudential rule, but the key to capturing the value of the future,” Di Stasi said, adding that the bank is responding to growing client demand and offering the product to Italian savers “for the very first time.” Built on notes sold in Germany and Austria Di Stasi said the bank is bringing to Italy “a pioneering model already proven by its success in Germany and Austria.” Those earlier notes are denominated in dollars and track BlackRock’s U.S.-listed iShares Bitcoin Trust instead. HypoVereinsbank, UniCredit’s German unit, sold a version to private clients in March with a 160% cap, or 60% upside. UniCredit Bank Austria launched its own six-year note in April with a 175% cap, or 75% upside. Italy’s 65% falls between the two. The bank has moved into bitcoin in steps. business.title: South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20%
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Unveils Crypto Bill Capping Exchange Ownership at 20% South Korea’s Financial Services Commission on Tuesday unveiled a government bill that would cap a major shareholder’s stake in a crypto exchange at 20%, open the door to domestic coin offerings and let bank-led groups issue won stablecoins. The draft, titled the Act on the Innovation of the Digital Asset Industry and Protection of Users, was presented at a Virtual Asset Committee meeting chaired by FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon. It would replace Korea’s two-track system, built on an anti-money-laundering law and a 2024 user protection act, with a single framework covering the industry, markets and users. Lee said the law would raise trust and transparency in Korea’s digital asset market and help draw new money into the industry. He said the government would do everything it can to see the bill fully debated in the National Assembly and enacted quickly. A 20% ownership cap for exchanges Under the bill, exchanges would become “digital asset platform operators,” a designation reserved for firms that hold separate licenses for dealing, brokerage and custody. The FSC modeled the ownership limit on the rules for alternative trading systems in the stock market. Major shareholders could own up to 20%, or up to 34% with FSC approval under a presidential decree. Shares above the limit would lose their voting rights. Existing exchanges would get three years after designation to comply, and small and midsize exchanges could get up to three more. The cap could reach some of Korea’s best-known exchanges. Mirae Asset Consulting owns 97.15% of Digital X, the exchange formerly known as Korbit, The Korea Herald reported . Naver Financial’s planned share-swap takeover of Dunamu, the operator of Upbit, would make the exchange a wholly owned subsidiary. The FSC declined to comment on specific companies, the paper said. “Ownership restrictions are necessary to strengthen exchanges’ public accountability and neutrality,” Yoo Young-jun, director general of the FSC’s Digital Financial Policy Bureau, said at a briefing, citing more than 10 million exchange accounts in Korea. The bill would also move trade execution, listing reviews and market surveillance from self-regulation to formal rules. Exchanges would need outside directors to make up a majority of their boards, plus audit committees and compliance officers. Coin offerings and won stablecoins Domestic initial coin offerings would be allowed as long as issuers file a white paper with the FSC before marketing tokens to the public. The release pointed to a platform company that sidestepped Korea’s ICO ban by setting up a foundation abroad, then sold its token through local exchanges. business.title: DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Moves to Forfeit $1.1 Billion in USDC Stolen in Binance Hack The Justice Department filed a civil forfeiture complaint Monday to take ownership of more than $1.1 billion in USDC that North Korean hackers stole from Binance last month, tokens that Circle froze but says it cannot move. The complaint , filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, targets all USDC held at 36 addresses across 18 blockchains. The department said the U.S. has now helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion in crypto from multiple sources since the Oct. 29 theft. On Nov. 12, the department said it had court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion, out of a joint government and industry freeze of more than $2.7 billion. A temporary restraining order issued that day was served on Circle the same day. Monday’s filing is the step that would let the government take title to the funds. Circle will mint replacement tokens Circle blocked access to the USDC on or about Oct. 29, the complaint says. But the stablecoin issuer told prosecutors it does not have the technical ability to transfer the tokens out of the blocklisted addresses, which remain under the hackers’ control. Instead, Circle has agreed to issue new USDC equal to the frozen amount and send it to the U.S. once a court enters a forfeiture order. The complaint calls those tokens “Substitute USDC.” Several of the addresses are smart contract and hot wallet addresses on Binance’s own platform. The hackers took them over in the attack and drained some, but not all, of the funds before Circle stepped in, prosecutors wrote. “It appears Binance no longer controlled them,” the complaint says. How the Binance hack worked The filing also lays out how investigators say the breach began. A Binance employee contacted by a purported recruiter agreed to a job interview and was told to download software that contained malware, which matches what the exchange said earlier this month. The infected device let the attackers plant an EIP-7702 injection. That feature, added to Ethereum in a 2025 upgrade, lets ordinary wallets temporarily act like smart contracts. Prosecutors said the hackers used it to take control of Binance’s hot wallets and route funds to a “sweeper” contract that moved them out as soon as they arrived. The first large transfer, about $780 million in USDC, left Binance on Ethereum at about 4:41 p.m. ET on Oct. 29, the complaint says. Another $43 million followed 18 minutes later. Investigators also traced AVAX that was split up, bridged and swapped until it became about $1.56 million in USDC. U.S. agencies attribute the theft to North Korean military hackers known as the Lazarus Group, or APT38. Investigators said some wallets that collected Binance funds also received money from the roughly $387 million Bitget hack in September, which the exchange’s CEO tied to North Korea. entertainment.description: Williams Alamu marks his B.Sc. First-Class Honours graduation in Statistics from the University of Ibadan. There was a time when Williams Alamu would rather not sit an examination than risk getting a grade he wasn’t happy with. A B or a C in his Cambridge A-levels felt like a possibility he wasn’t ready to entertain, so he didn’t write the exams. A few years later, at 23, he has graduated from the University of Ibadan with a B.Sc. in Statistics, First-Class Honours and a CGPA of 3.65/4.0. Somewhere along the way, he decided that fear was no longer going to make his decisions for him. When Williams got into UI, he had a rather ambitious plan: become the Best Graduating Student in his faculty. Getting there would require more than good intentions. There were 5:30am wake-ups, difficult Statistics courses, friends who became unofficial tutors, a ChatGPT Pro subscription in 300 level, job offers he turned down and one Demography exam that kept him awake for 36 hours. University, as it turns out, came with quite a few plot twists. In this interview with BellaNaija, Williams takes us through the habits, people and decisions that shaped his academic journey. He also tells us whether he got that coveted top spot, what he learnt from the opportunities he put on hold, and what he would tell another student hoping to graduate with First-Class Honours. I knew becoming the overall Best Graduating Student in the university would require an extraordinary amount of work, but I felt being the best in my faculty was something I wanted to work towards. And, of course, that would also mean graduating as the best student in my department. The motivation behind that goal goes back to shortly after secondary school, when my parents enrolled me in a Cambridge A-level programme. entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. sports.title: The USMNT needs Copa América. What it doesn't need is another home game
sports.description: USA fans look on from the stands during the CONMEBOL Copa America match between the United States and Boliva on June 23, 2024 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Copa América, South American soccer’s pride and joy, is returning to the U.S. in 2028 because organizers remain spellbound by the ticket sales and marketing success of the 2024 edition here. Tuesday’s announcement is a positive development for the U.S. team, which, for competitive reasons, desperately needs a break from the monotony of CONCACAF before the 2030 World Cup. Only so much is gained from fiddling with neighbors over and over again. Assuming the U.S. qualifies next summer, Copa América will furnish its to-be-announced head coach with pressure-packed, consequential matches in a prestigious tournament against different types of opponents. That’s a welcome change from the Nations Leagues and biennial Gold Cups, which are starting to feel like watching “Friends” reruns on Nick at Nite. But here’s where this Copa news falls short for the U.S. program: It’s in the U.S. again. Yes, the team needs to play in Copa América, but what it really needs is to play in it in South America. It needs to step out of its comfort zone of sterile hotels and stadiums. It needs to say goodbye to family and friends, experience new training and playing environments, and feel the heat of stepping into Rio de Janeiro’s Maracanã or Buenos Aires’ El Monumental to play the host team. True, the U.S. often feels like the visiting team at home when it tangles with Latin American opponents boasting a passionate diaspora. But the players still enjoy the predictability of home logistics, travel patterns, security and general nationwide support. That is not what they need right now. They need to suffer. Consider this: The U.S. hardly ever plays outside its borders, an arrangement that many might argue has left the program soft heading into World Cups. Talent, tactics and such are part of why the U.S. has stumbled in the round of 16 in its past four appearances, but mental toughness in the pressure-cookers of knockout soccer can’t be dismissed either. The location of matches is often out of the U.S.’s control. For revenue purposes, CONCACAF has staged every Nations League final four and almost every Gold Cup in the States. CONMEBOL, which oversees South American soccer, has shifted Copa América — the oldest international tournament in the world — to the U.S. three of the past five times after staging the first 44 editions in its own continent. The U.S. does have a say in the location of friendlies. Here again, though, the team is not facing the rigors of playing away matches. It has played 16 consecutive friendlies in FIFA windows at home since a visit to Mexico in October 2024. Going back to 2022, the number grows to 28 of 31. sports.title: Scarlett Schremmer Disqualified From Annika Debut After Lying
sports.description: Michael Madrid-Imagn Images The 19-year-old University of Miami sophomore received a rare sponsor exemption to The Annika driven by Gainbridge, only to disqualify herself by lying about a yardage book. She claimed she never used the illegal green-reading material when officials first asked, but photographic evidence proved otherwise. Golfmagic reported the disqualification came Saturday after the tour saw clear images of her consulting the prohibited book during the round. The book itself was legal in college golf, which explains why it sat in her bag, but it carries zero weight on the professional tour. Schremmer missed the cut before the ruling dropped, yet the lie turned a missed opportunity into a scandal. Her mother, former LPGA player Patricia Ehrhart, caddied for her, adding a layer of personal pressure that clearly backfired. Social media saw playing partner Perrine Delacour publicly challenge the tournament’s rule breach handling, causing the situation to become messy. The Lie That Sealed Her Fate Officials were alerted to the issue after the opening round, yet Schremmer kept playing on Friday before the truth came out. She initially told officials the book was not in use, a claim she later admitted was false in a Friday Instagram post. Schremmer wrote, “I had no idea that I had a yardage book with illegal Information. When I was approached about it, I was scared, embarrassed, and made an extremely poor decision in saying it was not in use.” That panic cost her the chance to show her skills against the best women in the world. Delacour, who partnered Schremmer for the first two rounds, took to X to ask, “Can we talk about the yardage [book] illegal and LPGA trust the sponsor invite over 2 LPGA players and 2 caddies.” The French veteran confirmed she spoke directly to rules officials about the violation, highlighting how the amateur status of the invitee complicated the situation. The LPGA Tour stated the rule requires players to use only approved books throughout their round, and photo evidence showed Schremmer violated that mandate. Trust Is Hard To Build Back With two fall college tournament wins and a USGA 2026 Elite Amateur Program spot secured, Schremmer held the 51st rank in the World Amateur Golf Ranking. Those credentials meant nothing once she chose to hide the truth. While Schremmer’s Friday admission signaled a move from denial to accountability, the harm remains irreversible. She stated in her post, according to Yahoo, “I deeply regret that, I always will, and I want to own that mistake.”

sports.description: Manthey racing�s Porsche 911 (911) is a blur of speed up from turn 5 during practice at the Motul SportsCar Endurance Grand Prix Featuring IMSA, Friday, July 31, 2026, at Road America near Elkhart Lake, Wis. Tsunami RT is heading to the United States to race. The San Marino-based team will field a Porsche 911 GT3 R in the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup starting in 2027. This move brings a new name to the GTD class and adds depth to the five-race schedule. Team principal Valerio M. Speziali wants to build a lasting presence in North America. He sees the US market as a place to grow the team’s skills over time. “We are delighted to join the IMSA Michelin Endurance Cup next year, giving us the chance to build our experience and grow in endurance racing season by season,” Speziali said, according to Speedway Digest . The group knows the competition is fierce, but they are not backing down. “We know how competitive the GTD field is and we’re ready to fight for strong results from the opening round,” he added according to Speedway Digest. A Driver Mix Built for Endurance The car will carry the number 79 and feature a mix of veterans and fresh talent. Fabio Babini leads the group with deep roots in IMSA history. He won the GTU class at the 2000 Rolex 24 and took the GT title at Le Mans in 2001. His last start in the WeatherTech Championship was back in 2019, but he knows the track well. Matteo Cressoni brings recent experience with 13 starts between 2015 and 2025 in various GT cars. Two new faces will make their debut in 2027. Alex Fontana and Johannes Zelger have raced together for Tsunami RT in the Intercontinental GT Challenge during the 2026 season. The team will rotate drivers based on the race length. They plan to use a three-driver lineup for the Sebring, Glen, Road America, and Road Atlanta events. This strategy helps manage the physical toll of long races while keeping speed high. Adding a new Porsche entry changes the dynamic of the GTD class. The field is already crowded with top-tier teams, and every new car adds pressure. Babini’s resume shows the team is not just playing for participation. He has won at the highest levels of sports car racing. His experience in the GRAND-AM series and American Le Mans Series gives the team a solid foundation. Cressoni has also seen action in Ferrari and Lamborghini entries, proving he can handle different machines. The Rolex 24 holds special weight for this organization. Speziali called the chance to see the team on the entry list a major milestone. It is not just about finishing the race. It is about proving that a European team can succeed in the tough US endurance scene. The 2027 season will show if they have the pace to match the big names. sports.title: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato
sports.description: Phillies offseason is looking bleak after missing out on Teruaki Sato originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Two days before Thanksgiving, the Philadelphia Phillies have not made a significant roster move of any kind. The December 1 lockout is looming, and the Phillies are beginning to run out of time to make moves. But it's not just the time crunch making things tricky for the Phillies. They've already lost out on Teruaki Sato, easily the best free-agent option the Phillies could've landed this Fall. He's headed to the Chicago Cubs on a six-year, $120 million deal. After missing out on Sato, what now for the Phillies' offseason plans? The Athletic's Charlotte Varnes and Matt Gelb shared an update on just that, and it's looking like the Phillies could be in for quite the bleak offseason. Phillies might be in for a bleak offseason after missing out on Teruaki Sato After missing out on Sato, it would seem natural for the Phillies to look towards Seiya Suzuki and/or Randy Arozarena as free-agent outfield options. But, as The Athletic duo pointed out, there are problems with both. "The Phillies would have to sacrifice draft picks and international bonus money to sign either outfielder because both were extended qualifying offers," Varnes and Gelb write. "They may wait to sign until the labor situation is resolved." There's just one problem with that line of thinking: "If Arozarena's market develops in the next week, though, the Phillies will not have the luxury of waiting," Varnes and Gelb write. MORE : Blue Jays miss out on another premier free agent with Mets' Tarik Skubal news Between the loss of draft picks and international bonus pool money, and the potentially rushed nature of a Suzuki or Arozarena deal, the Phillies might not be the landing spots for either right-handed hitting outfielder. So, if they aren't a perfect suitor for an outfielder, what about a pitcher to upgrade the bullpen? Unfortunately, things aren't looking good there either. "They could focus on pitching, but the Phillies, according to multiple league sources, are not considered serious players for the top free-agent reliever, Adrian Morejon," Gelb and Varnes report. Adrian Morejon would've been an awesome pickup as a setup man for Jhoan Duran. But a deal isn't looking likely. With issues signing someone like Suzuki or Arozarena, and their lack of strong interest in Morejon, what could they actually do this offseason? Trading for players might prove tricky, as The Athletic duo notes the Phillies "will be protective of their top prospects." Thanks to their weaker farm system as seen by the rest of MLB, if the Phillies aren't willing to part with their top prospects, getting a trade through for a good player isn't very likely

sports.title: Blue Jays land Japanese star pitcher Kaima Taira on $80M deal
sports.description: Blue Jays signing The Blue Jays landed a starting pitcher for roughly one-sixth the price of Tarik Skubal. After losing to the Mets in the Skubal sweepstakes, the Blue Jays pivoted and are signing Japanese righty Kaima Taira to a five-year, $80 million deal, The Post’s Jon Heyman first reported . The deal includes an opt-out clause after the third year, per Heyman. Kaima Taira of the Seibu Lions celebrates setting an NPB record with 39 consecutive scoreless games in Fukuoka, Japan, Thursday, July 1, 2021. /Kyodo News via AP The starting pitching dominos are falling in free agency ahead of the expected Dec. 1 lockout, with Skubal serving as the catalyst by signing his nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets . The Blue Jays made a competitive nine-year, $420 million offer for Skuba l, but he opted for $30 million more to head to Flushing. Freddy Peralta agreed to a five-year, $125 million deal with the Orioles on Tuesday, and the pitching-needy Blue Jays swooped in to land the talented 27-year-old Taira. Taira has experience as a reliever and starter, and spent the past season with the Seibu Lions of the Japan Pacific League as a starter. He posted a 1.54 ERA spanning 23 outings, pitching 146 innings and striking out 141 batters. Taira walked 45 batters but allowed just four homers. The year prior, he made 54 appearances and tallied 52 2/3 innings while posting a 2.05 ERA. He owns a career 1.85 ERA in his nine seasons pitching in Japan, according to Baseball Reference. “His stuff and release characteristics are what is intriguing to evaluators. His fastball sits 94-97 mph and hits 100 mph with his four-seam fastball, the headliner in an eight-pitch mix: sinker, changeup, splitter, cutter, slider, sweeper, and curveball,” according to ESPN . “Taira achieves a unique low release and advantageous angle for his fastball with his outlier extension (roughly a foot more than his 5-foot-8 stature) and lower than average arm slot.” The Blue Jays now have a solid rotation featuring AL Cy Young runner-up Dylan Cease, Taira, midseason trade acquisition righty Joel Soriano and talented youngster Trey Yesavage. They reportedly are also in the mix for offensive help and their representatives met with Jazz Chisholm Jr. earlier in free agency. Toronto finished in last place in the AL East last year following its run to the World Series in 2025.

Ryan Jeffers secured the first windfall of cash by accepting the qualifying offer at $23.15 million for 2027. Sonny Gray then returned to the franchise on a two-year deal worth $55 million. Walters still expects Pohlads to sell the Minnesota Twins After the 2024 season, the Pohlads gave Minnesota Twins fans the best news in years. They were exploring a sale . Then they pulled the team off the market before Tom Pohlad took over for his younger brother Joe. Since then, Tom has been adamant about the family’s plan to re-invest in the organization in ways that those before him have not. He has also downplayed any plans to put the team back up for sale after a new Collective Bargaining Agreement is reached. sports.title: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions
sports.description: CTA president wants to rebuild relationship with Real Madrid amid refereeing tensions Fran Soto, president of Spain’s Technical Committee of Referees (CTA), has expressed his desire to improve relations with Real Madrid amid ongoing tensions. Los Blancos have been vociferous in their complaints about the refereeing in Spain as well as the Negreira scandal involving Barcelona, leading to a lot of tension between the club and the governing bodies. Soto wants to move on from the Negreira scandal Speaking to the media at the first Refereeing Gala, Soto addressed the ongoing tensions surrounding the refereeing in Spain and Real Madrid’s complaints, in particular. The CTA president defended the refereeing community over the fallout from the Negreira scandal and called for the focus to shift towards restoring normality. “The referees are the ones most harmed by a person who was vice president of the Technical Committee of Referees,” Soto said, as quoted by SPORT . Real Madrid are unhappy with the refereeing in Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Soto insisted that officials have suffered the consequences of the controversy and argued that they cannot remain trapped by events from the past. ”We mustn’t dwell on the past; we have to move forward and continue refereeing, put it behind us, and look to the future,” he added. Soto questions Real Madrid’s VAR statistics Soto was also asked about the presentation made by Real Madrid during the club’s recent assembly , wherein they showed that VAR had ruled out 42 of their goals since the technology was introduced, compared to 19 for Barcelona. Real Madrid president Florentino Perez used the figures to reinforce the club’s complaints about what it considers unfavourable refereeing treatment. Real Madrid have made multiple complaints over the officiating. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) Soto declined to engage in a direct confrontation with Real Madrid but questioned whether the figures, on their own, could support the conclusions being drawn. “Every club defends its position. I don’t agree that this objective data can be used to draw conclusions,” he stated. However, the CTA president made clear that he has no intention of escalating the dispute and would prefer to see communication between the two sides return to normal. “I don’t want to get into a dispute with any club, least of all with Madrid. I hope that in the future we can resolve this situation,” he concluded.

sports.title: IMSA Cuts Testing Days: A Smart Move For The 2027 Season
sports.description: The No. 52 LMP2 Inter Europol ORECA of Nick Boulle and Tom Dolman drives through the Carousel during the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship race Sunday, August 4, 2024, at Road America in Elkhart Lake, Wisconsin. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect IMSA is finally cutting the fat off the testing schedule for the 2027 WeatherTech SportsCar Championship. The new sporting regulations announced Tuesday hit the top teams the hardest, but they might be exactly what the series needs to level the playing field. The rules eliminate all private testing for GTD Pro entries outside of sanctioned events. GTP teams now get only two manufacturer test days per season, with team-specific days removed entirely. According to Sportscar365 , these restrictions come alongside new licensed tests at Sebring and Road Atlanta that are open to every team. The move stops deep-pocketed teams from hoarding track time and forces everyone to rely on their actual race strategy. Inter Europol Doubles Down Anyway While the rulebook tightens, one team is betting big on its own talent. For the 2027 season, Inter Europol Competition revealed plans to run two full-time ORECA LMP2 07 entries. This expansion adds a second car to their existing No. 43 program, creating a formidable two-car assault on the title. The team manager, Sascha Fassbender, said, “We are very happy to have two cars committed to the full IMSA season with two strong driver lineups.” Inter Europol is not backing down from the challenge despite the reduced testing window. The team aims to fight for the championship with both cars, building on a close 2026 title race. Following their second-place finish last year, Jeremy Clarke and Tom Dillmann are back for the flagship No. 43 car. Clarke noted their drive to win, stating, “We came so close last year, so we’re even more motivated to finish on the top step at the end of the season.” Testing Limits Will Test Team Depth The new regulations also slash test days for LMP2 and GTD teams, cutting LMP2 allocation from 12 days down to eight. GTD teams see their days drop from six to two, though FIA Bronze-rated drivers still get two extra days. According to Sportscar365, private testing is now banned during a 120-day blackout period preceding major events like Daytona and Sebring. This forces teams to be sharper with their limited track time. Inter Europol’s new No. 343 entry brings in fresh firepower with drivers Nick Yelloly and Daniel Goldburg. Goldburg brings experience from racing against the team for three years in LMP2. He summed up his move to the organization with a simple phrase: “If you can’t beat them, join them.” The team has also added INDYCAR driver Nolan Siegel for the Rolex 24 at Daytona lineup. The 2027 season will start with a sanctioned test at Daytona International Speedway on December 10 and 11.

sports.title: Mystery grows over ex-Met, actor Lance Broadway’s sudden death after police report: ‘Unexplained’
sports.description: Lance Broadway The police report related to Lance Broadway’s death is providing far more questions about the former Mets pitcher and Hollywood actor’s passing than it is answers. Broadway died at 43 years old on Nov. 17 in an apartment complex stairwell in Dallas, Texas, and law enforcement appears to be stumped by how he ended up that way, according to a Dallas Police Department incident report obtained by the California Post on Tuesday. Actor Lance Broadway arrives at a special screening of “The Iceman” at ArcLight Hollywood in Hollywood, California, Monday, April 22, 2013. Getty Images Authorities called the matter an “unexplained death (no offense)” in the document, adding that there were no signs that Broadway was under the influence of alcohol or drugs. The “narrative information” section of the report was heavily redacted, though it did note that the person who reported the situation to cops observed Broadway “to be deceased sitting on the stairwell of the call location.” Lance Broadway of the New York Mets walks back to the mound against the Atlanta Braves in New York, Monday, Sept. 21, 2009. Jeff Zelevansky Police were called to the scene at 5:56 p.m., according to the incident report, and Broadway was formally pronounced dead at 6:20 p.m., per the Dallas County Medical Examiner. The cause of death remains undetermined as autopsy results are still pending, the Dallas County Medical Examiner stated. Lance Broadway #41 of the Chicago White Sox pitches during a game against the Kansas City Royals at U.S. Cellular Field in Chicago, Aug. 14, 2008. MLB Photos via Getty Images Broadway, a first-round pick in the 2005 MLB draft, pitched for the White Sox and Mets from 2007 to 2009, and in retirement, he got into acting. The 6-foot-2 right-handed pitcher garnered roles in several popular movies and TV shows, including “Olympus Has Fallen,” “Lucifer” and “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.”

sports.title: 'It's impossible to make an analysis' - Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca admits Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd are a mystery ahead of Champions League clash
sports.description: Fenerbahce v OL Lyonnes - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 Play-Offs First Leg - Getty Images Sport Sporting boss Paulo Fonseca says it is "impossible to make an analysis" of Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United ahead of Wednesday's Champions League clash in Lisbon. With Leny Yoro sent off after eight minutes at Anfield, Fonseca has turned to footage of Pochettino's time with the United States, while refusing to label the Red Devils "fragile". Fonseca in the dark over Pochettino's United Fonseca has admitted he has little to go on when preparing for United, with Pochettino having taken charge of only one game. That match, a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool, was disrupted by Yoro's early red card, which has since been overturned on appeal. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," Fonseca said, as reported by BBC Sport . "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." Fonseca refuses to label United 'fragile' Despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Fonseca refused to accept that they are vulnerable. "I don't follow the reasoning," he said. "Manchester is a great team. I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile." He pointed to United's last Champions League outing, when they came from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day," he added. United's domestic slump United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their last six matches, leaving Pochettino with a huge task after replacing Michael Carrick during the international break. Fonseca, who was appointed on November 4 after Sporting bought him out of his contract at Lyon, is also new to his role and has had little time to stamp his own ideas on the side. Defender Eduardo Quaresma has already warned his team-mates against underestimating United . Lisbon showdown awaits Sporting host United at the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Wednesday night, with Yoro cleared to play. Pochettino will be desperate for a positive result to ease the pressure after a chaotic start to his reign.

sports.title: Detroit Lions lose rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard for the season
sports.description: The Detroit Lions have lost another player to a season-ending injury on their defense. Lions coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday, Nov. 24, that rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard will miss the rest of the season after injuring his knee in last week’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Gill-Howard was hurt on a goal-line offensive snap, where’s he’s played at times as a jumbo tight end this season, late in the game. “Hate that for him,” Campbell said. “He’s had a heck of a season up to this point.” A sixth-round pick out of Texas Tech, Gill-Howard has played as the Lions’ No. 3 defensive tackle this season and been one of their best interior pass rushers. He has 11 tackles, six quarterback hits and two sacks. Gill-Howard’s injury is the second major setback on the defensive line and third to the unit this month. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell is out for the season with a spinal cord injury he suffered in a Nov. 1 win over the Minnesota Vikings, and Pro Bowl defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore the ACL in his right knee while celebrating a sack in the Lions’ win over the New England Patriots in Germany two weeks ago. Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams and Gill-Howard have played the bulk of the snaps at defensive tackle for the Lions this season, but Campbell said he’s confident in the team’s depth at the position. Big ends Tyler Lacy and Levi Onwuzurike can play inside, Mekhi Wingo could see his first action of the season and practice squad linemen Aidan Keanaaina and Taki Taimani are candidates to play in the Lions’ Thanksgiving game this week against the Chicago Bears. The Lions and Bears are 8-2 and ties for first place in the NFC North. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Detroit Lions lose rookie DT Skyler Gill-Howard for the season

sports.title: “100%” – Liverpool receive boost in race for €50m January signing
sports.description: “100%” – Liverpool receive boost in race for €50m January signing Alejandro Balde Transfer Latest: Liverpool Monitoring Barcelona Exit as €50m January Fee Emerges Liverpool are among the clubs tracking Alejandro Balde ahead of the January transfer window, with fresh reporting indicating the Barcelona left-back is expected to leave and could cost as much as €50 million. The update comes via Juan Jesus, who states: “Despite Deco’s words, Alejandro Balde is 100% out. Several clubs know this and are closely monitoring his situation, including Manchester United, PSG, AC Milan and Liverpool,” before adding, “Barça expects the bidding to drive up the price and is confident of securing his departure for at least 45-50 million euros.” That information places Liverpool firmly in the conversation around one of the more intriguing defensive situations developing before the market reopens. Balde has long been viewed as a high-level talent, and any indication that Barcelona are prepared to sanction a sale will naturally alert a number of elite sides across Europe. Liverpool transfer plans sharpen into focus For Liverpool, the key question is whether genuine interest turns into concrete action. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle. That's not particularly low for a sports car, but it's practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. So, for the company's first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver.
